results.knownDifference: The tag comparison is constant time; ct-verify measures it directly and shows no difference. What differs is that the failure path zeroizes the output buffer and the success path does not. That branch is on whether the tag verified, which the caller already learns from the returned error, so it reveals nothing about the key or the plaintext. It is not free, though: a caller trying to hide whether authentication failed -- to deny an attacker a decryption oracle -- cannot assume this is invisible, and should add its own constant-time handling above this layer.
results.verdict: differs, for a documented and public reason
